summary: Streaming chat connection ends silently during peak utilization in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports streaming chat sessions (SSE and websocket) dropping to a silent closed state mid-response when overall capacity in the dedicated GPU pool is high. The stream shows steady bytes then connection is closed by server with no final token or error payload.

Impact:
- ScaleChat reports 8-12% of long (>15s) streaming responses in eu-west are cut off or closed abruptly during peak windows; user-facing experience: partial replies with no retry token.
- Affects production customers on dedicated pools using vicuna-13b family.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (committed GPUs) in eu-west.
- Model: redwood/vicuna-13b-openai-like (pinned by customer).
- Client types: SSE (EventSource) and WebSocket.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Open a streaming chat request with long generation target (200-800 tokens).
2) Keep generating during 15:00-17:00 UTC (peak).
3) Observe stream producing tokens for ~20-40s then abruptly close (client receives close/no final chunk).

Observed behavior:
- No explicit 5xx returned to client before closure. Socket reports abnormal close (code 1006) for Ws; SSE client sees connection close without last "data: [DONE]".
- Server-side worker logs show SIGKILL or worker process ended around same timestamp for some sessions.

Expected behavior:
- Stream continues until generation completes or returns clear error payload with retry/resume token.

Relevant logs/headers (redacted):
- Proxy keepalive: OK.
- Example server log lines:
  [2026-03-12T16:11:23Z] stream_session_id=abc123 status=producing token_count=124
  [2026-03-12T16:11:55Z] stream_session_id=abc123 status=producing token_count=238
  [2026-03-12T16:11:56Z] scheduler:eviction action=terminate target=worker-17 reason=memory_pressure priority=low session=abc123
  [2026-03-12T16:11:56Z] worker-17 exit_code=137 pid=15234

Attachments:
- Customer provided client timestamps and SDK logs (attached).
comments: 2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage - acknowledged with customer, requested SDK logs and session ids. Notified SRE on-call.
2026-03-12 - Customer (ScaleChat): Provided 12 example session ids and SDK logs showing abrupt close at 16:11-16:17 UTC. Confirmed impact window aligns with their traffic spikes.
2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Investigating - observed correlated scheduler eviction events in eu-west dedicated pool. Opening follow-up internal ticket INT-1182 for scheduler config review.

2026-03-13 - Liam O'Connor: Found pattern - when GPU memory pressure is high the scheduler preempted workers running streaming sessions labeled with low priority; preemption used SIGKILL sequence which left no graceful error to propagate to client. Reproduced in staging with load-generator and long streams.

2026-03-13 - Support (Aisha): Shared mitigation steps with customer: 1) enable session_priority=high in their routing profile to avoid preemption, 2) enable client-side resume token handling. Customer applied session_priority change for a subset of requests for testing.

2026-03-13 - Engineering (Liam): Deployed hotfix to scheduler (PR 290) to reserve N streaming slots per GPU and to change preemption signal to graceful-terminate then forced-kill after delay. Deployed runtime patch v1.12.3 to ensure worker returns error payload before exit when possible.

2026-03-13 - Customer (ScaleChat): Verified reduced occurrence in subset; long streams continued through peak for sessions with session_priority=high. Observed remaining failures drop from ~10% to ~1%.
2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Confirming resolution and recommending closing ticket. Advised customer to keep session_priority for streaming endpoints and upgrade to runtime v1.12.3.
investigation_notes: Correlated customer session timestamps with scheduler logs and worker exit codes (exit_code=137 indicates OOM or forced kill).
Reproduced in staging by simulating mixed workload: streaming long generations + background batch finetune jobs causing transient memory pressure.

Root cause hypothesis: scheduler allowed low-priority streaming sessions to be preempted immediately under memory pressure; preemption used immediate kill which prevented runtime from flushing final token/error to the client.
Observed that SSE/WebSocket clients do not receive a server-side error when process is killed; proxy connection close occurs without final chunk.
Mitigation validated: reserving streaming slots and making preemption graceful preserves client-visible error or completes generation.
resolution: Mitigations applied: 1) Scheduler change merged (PR 290) to reserve 4 streaming slots per GPU and to send SIGTERM to workers before SIGKILL; 2) Runtime v1.12.3 deployed which attempts to emit final error frames on graceful termination; 3) Customer advised to set session_priority=high on critical streaming routes and to upgrade SDK to support resume tokens. Post-deploy verification in eu-west shows failures reduced from ~10% to ~1% for ScaleChat. Follow-up item: scheduler autoscaler policy will be updated (INT-1182) to avoid evicting active streams during scale-down windows.
closure_notes: 2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Customer confirmed acceptance of fix and will monitor for one week. No further immediate actions requested.
2026-03-14 - Liam O'Connor: Monitoring dashboards set to alert on stream-eviction-rate > 0.5% and linked to #sre on-call channel.
Postmortem pointer: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Streaming+Eviction+Postmortem (to be populated by on-call)
Ticket resolved after customer verification and monitoring thresholds established.
